![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14149458/assets/555eec8e88dd658903e19b8779f85598f57126b054d5058b662824f09de0f6cb.png)

Consider the region $D$ shown above. If 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-x, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}({y}^{2}-x)\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

I. $R=[-1,1]\times [-1,1]$

II. $R=[-1,1]\times [-1,2]$

III. $R=[-2,2]\times [-1,0]$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-x, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}({y}^{2}-x)\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given rectangles.

- Rectangles I and III do not cover the region $D.$

- Rectangle II covers the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
